root_cause.text: On uniprocessor (UP) kernels, `spin_trylock()` is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when a lock is already held, allowing `kmalloc_nolock()` called from NMI context to re-enter the slab allocator and corrupt the slab state by acquiring `n->list_lock` already held by the interrupted context.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a check `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` to `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` in `mm/slub.c` to prevent re-entry into the slab allocator on UP kernels during an NMI.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent kmalloc allocations in NMI context on uniprocessor systems to avoid lock re-entrancy issues.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check to return NULL if the system is uniprocessor (non-SMP) and the execution context is a Non-Maskable Interrupt (NMI).
intent_record.how: Prevents kmalloc execution in NMI context on UP systems, avoiding re-entrancy bugs caused by spin_trylock() always succeeding on uniprocessor configurations.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent kmalloc allocations in NMI context on uniprocessor systems to avoid lock re-entrancy issues.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent directly addresses the vulnerability by preventing kmalloc allocations in NMI context on uniprocessor systems, which avoids the lock re-entrancy issue described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This condition only prevents NMI and hardirq allocations when CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is enabled. On uniprocessor (UP) kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op, meaning NMI context allocations can re-enter the slab allocator and corrupt the slab state even without CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT. Thus, NMI allocations must be blocked on UP kernels as well.
